transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Lee, I'm here because... well, I'm pretty sure the people on this environmental modeling contract I'm working on have been tracking my revisions. And not just tracking them, but actually planting errors in the datasets. It's like they're trying to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, but I know what I'm seeing.

Alongside these concerns about your coworkers, have you noticed any big changes in your mood or energy—like feeling unusually elated, irritable, or full of energy, or on the other hand feeling very down, hopeless, or low on energy?

No, not really. I mean... my energy is fine. I haven't felt unusually high or deeply depressed or anything like that. I'm just... well, I'm frustrated. It's stressful dealing with this contract situation, having to constantly double-check the math because you can't trust the people you work with. But as far as my actual mood or energy going way up or down... no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Have you ever heard voices, or seen or sensed things that other people around you don't seem to notice?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices, and I'm not seeing things that aren't there. 

It's really just the data... the numbers in the models that are being altered. I don't have any strange visions or hear people talking to me when nobody is around. Everything I'm seeing is right there on the screen in the datasets.
How long have you been noticing and worrying about these changes to your data—days, weeks, or months?

It's been going on for about two months now. That's when I really became certain that they were tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets. Before that, maybe I brushed it off, but for the last two months, I've been sure of it.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions recently, or are you using any new medications, drugs, or alcohol, that started around the same time these concerns about your coworkers began?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been to a doctor recently, so no new diagnoses or anything. I don't take any medications, and I don't really drink... maybe a beer every now and then, but that's it. No drugs, either. There's nothing physical going on with me, and nothing I'm taking that would cause this. Like I said, it's just the numbers on the screen.

Outside of this specific concern about your coworkers and the data, how have things been going for you at work and at home—are you still managing your usual responsibilities and relationships as well as before?

Honestly, not great. I've... I've fallen pretty far behind on the modeling deliverables at work. It got bad enough that the firm actually reassigned pieces of the contract to other people. And the junior analysts I'm supposed to supervise—I've basically stopped being useful to them right now. I just can't focus on their stuff. 

And at home... I mostly just keep to myself. My wife has had to really push me lately just to keep basic routines going, you know, normal daily stuff. So, no, I guess I'm not really managing things the way I used to.

Besides your concerns about the data, have you or others noticed any changes in how you speak or organize your thoughts, or a decrease in your emotional expression or motivation for everyday activities?

I don't think my speech has changed, or how I organize my thoughts, but... yeah, the motivation is definitely gone. 

These days I can just sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with my telescope still covered up. I know I used to really enjoy things like hiking, mentoring the younger analysts at work, going to astronomy nights... but lately, I just don't feel much pull to start anything. I don't really have the drive to talk to anyone, either. I just kind of sit there.

This loss of motivation and pulling away from activities—did that start around the same two months ago when you first became certain about the data tampering, or did it begin separately, and has it been continuous since then?

No, it didn't start with the data thing two months ago. It's been going on a lot longer than that. 

This whole decline... I guess you could call it that... it really started after I was put in charge of the larger environmental modeling contract. That was about two years and two months ago. Ever since then, it's just been a steady slide, and it hasn't really stopped.

During this two-year period of decline, apart from the concerns about your coworkers altering the data, have you had any other unusual beliefs, suspicions about people or situations, or noticed things with your senses that others didn't seem to notice?

No, not really. It's just the data thing. I haven't seen or heard anything that wasn't there, or had any other strange ideas. It's really just been the lack of motivation and the situation with the modeling data at work. That's about it.
